body.p: Claims 16-24 are pending, with claim 16 being independent. Claim 16 is amended. Claims 1-15 are canceled.

The Office Action rejected Claims 16-24 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Chen (U.S. 2012/123222) in view of Zaleski (U.S 7,945,457). Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections, the characterizations of the pending claims and the cited references and each and every implicit and explicit potential for reliance on Official Notice. Solely in the interest of expediting prosecution, Applicant has amended the independent claim as shown above.

Chen simply teaches a smart phone and an ability to download phone apps. There is no teaching about a user having an ability to select another software's "health parameter" that is different or not available directly from the first software. In the Response to Arguments, the Examiner states that Chen teaches selecting a second software from an app store. Final Office Action, 4. However, selecting an app from an app store would just install an independent second software on Chen's phone. If the user wants to select a parameter from the second software, they would have to open the second software in Chen's system and then would have no access to the first software. In contrast, the claims here recite an ability to "select a determination of a health parameter that is specific to the second software" from the "first graphical user interface" that is provided by "the first software." Accordingly, the user does not have to exit the first software like they would in Chen to open a new app corresponding to the second software and lose accessing to processing of data from the first software. The advantages here are the that processing of the physiological parameters are done by the first software, which are then passed on to the second software in the background (if selected by the user), and the resulting "health parameter" is determined by the second software ("enabling the second software to execute the one or more post- processing functions on the determined one or more physiological parameters based on the selection of the second software, wherein the one or more post-processing functions are configured to determine the health parameter" as recited in the claim). The "health parameter" is displayed on "a second user interface" also generated by the first software. Therefore, the user never has to
open up the second software according to a non-limiting embodiment of pending claim unlike in Chen.

Zaleski teaches an applet viewer that enables user to monitor over a web browser. It is not teaching, for example, two applets, where the first applet is getting a health parameter from a second applet while first applet is running the user interface.
Accordingly, the combination fails to teach or suggest all the limitations of amended independent Claim 16.

The dependent claims are patentable for the same reasons articulated above with respect to their independent claims. The dependent claims are also patentable because of the additional features recited therein.

Although the present communication may include alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this application that previously pending claims are not patentable over the cited references. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application. Applicant reserves the right to pursue at a later date any previously pending or other broader or narrower claims that capture any subject matter supported by the present disclosure, including subject matter found to be specifically disclaimed herein or by any prior prosecution. Accordingly, reviewers of this or any parent, child or related prosecution history shall not reasonably infer that Applicant has made any disclaimers or disavowals of any subject matter supported by the present application. Further, Applicant's arguments in favor of one independent claim should not be imputed to any other independent claim.
Applicant wishes to draw the Examiner's attention to the following co-pending applications of the present application's assignee.

In view of the foregoing amendments and remarks, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the outstanding rejections and allow the present application. If any issues arise during examination, the Examiner is invited to call the undersigned representative at his direct dial number listed below.
By focusing on specific claims and claim recitations in the discussion above, Applicant does not intend to imply that other claim recitations are disclosed or rendered obvious by the art of record.
